pages.title: Disney Cruise Door Decoration Rules & Ideas (2026)
pages.description: Disney Cruise Line
pages.body: Disney Cruise Door Decoration Rules & Ideas (2026) | Cruising Cove Cruising Cove Ships Ports Dining Entertainment Excursions FAQ Community Marketplace Find an Agent Onboard traditions Decorating your stateroom door. A beloved DCL tradition, with a real rule change as of June 2026. Here's exactly what's allowed now. — Quick facts At a glance Rule updated May 28, 2026 Effective Sailings from June 3, 2026 Allowed Magnets only Not allowed Tape, hooks, adhesives Damage fee $100 per incident Wooden doors Concierge, Dream & Fantasy — What changed The June 2026 rule update Disney Cruise Line updated its door decoration policy on May 28, 2026, effective for sailings starting June 3, 2026. The core change: decorations now have to stay on your stateroom door only — no more spilling onto the hallway walls or ceiling around your door, which some guests had been doing more and more in recent years. Everything else about the tradition is unchanged. Magnetic decorations are still fully allowed, fish extenders are unaffected, and this remains one of the most fun, low-cost ways to personalize your stateroom before you even step inside. — The rules, plainly What's allowed and what's not Magnets: yes. DCL stateroom doors are magnetic surfaces (with one exception below), and character magnets, signs, and displays are the standard way to decorate. Tape, adhesives, hooks, suction cups: no. Anything that isn't magnetic risks damaging the door. Door only: yes. Hallway walls and ceiling: no. This is the new rule as of June 2026. Sound or video elements: no , as a courtesy to other guests in the corridor. Over-the-door organizers: no — these are explicitly prohibited. Damage a door decorating it improperly, and you're looking at a $100 fee per incident. — Worth knowing Concierge staterooms on the Disney Dream and Disney Fantasy have wooden doors, not magnetic ones — magnets simply won't stick. If you're in one of those rooms, a fish extender is your best option instead. — Sizing it right Door number plate sizes Every stateroom door has a built-in number plate you can decorate around. On the Magic, Wonder, Dream, and Fantasy, it's a circle roughly 7.5 inches in diameter. On the newer ships — Wish, Treasure, and Destiny — it's a curved-edge rectangle, roughly 4.5 by 7 inches. Many guests build their door magnet design around this shape, having a character "peek out" from behind the number plate. — Getting started Ideas within the new rules A large central character magnet sized to your door, with smaller magnets around it A "countdown" or cruise-number magnet if this isn't your first sailing Birthday, anniversary, or first-cruise celebration signage — all magnetic A family name banner across the top of the door Pack decorations in your carry-on, not checked luggage, so you can decorate as soon as you board — before checked bags typically arrive Cruising Cove Ships Ports Dining Entertainment Plan Your Sailing Find an Agent Cruising Cove is an independent planning guide and is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by The Walt Disney Company, Disney Cruise Line, or any of their affiliates. pages.title: Disney Cruise Excursions vs. Independent Tours
pages.description: Should you book Disney
pages.body: Disney Cruise Excursions vs. Independent Tours | Cruising Cove Cruising Cove Ships Ports Dining Entertainment Excursions FAQ Community Marketplace Find an Agent Port excursions Disney excursion, or go independent? Disney's own Port Adventures cost more than booking the same activity independently. Here's the actual tradeoff, and the one detail most people miss. — The real tradeoff It's not really about price Independent excursions are almost always cheaper than the identical activity booked through Disney — sometimes by 30–50%. That's the number everyone leads with, and it's true. But it's not the number that actually matters most. If you book through Disney and the excursion runs late, the ship waits for you. If you book independently and your tour runs late — traffic, a slow guide, a mechanical delay — the ship does not wait. You are responsible for getting yourself back to the port on time, and if you don't make it, you're on your own to catch up with the ship at the next port, at your own expense. For most families, that single fact is worth more than the savings. — When independent makes sense Independent tours are worth it when... The activity is close to the port with a wide time buffer built in You've read recent, verified reviews of the specific operator You're comfortable managing your own transportation and timing The price gap is large enough to matter for your budget — When Disney's own is worth it Disney Port Adventures are worth it when... You're traveling with young kids and want zero logistics risk It's a longer excursion (multi-hour, further from port) where a delay would be costly You value not having to research and vet an unfamiliar operator yourself Peace of mind is worth more to you than the price difference — Coming soon Side-by-side excursion comparisons — In progress Port-by-port comparisons of specific Disney Port Adventures against verified independent alternatives — with real price gaps and the ship-wait risk flagged for each — are being built out as this section grows. pages.description: The most common questions about Disney Cruise Line, answered plainly — passports, age requirements, alcohol policy, seasickness, what
pages.body: Disney Cruise Line FAQ | Cruising Cove Cruising Cove Ships Ports Dining Entertainment Excursions FAQ Community Marketplace Find an Agent Frequently asked The questions everyone actually asks. Real, commonly-asked questions about Disney Cruise Line, answered plainly — no fluff, no guessing. Do I need a passport for a Disney cruise? For "closed-loop" sailings — cruises that depart from and return to the same U.S. port — U.S. citizens technically only need a certified birth certificate with a raised seal plus a government-issued photo ID (for guests 16+). A passport is still strongly recommended even when not required — it's the only document accepted if you need to fly home unexpectedly from a port, and it simplifies re-entry to the U.S. For any cruise that isn't closed-loop (international one-way sailings, repositioning cruises), a passport is required for all ages, including infants. What's the minimum age to sail? For most itineraries, guests must be at least 6 months old at the time of embarkation. For certain repositioning cruises (South Pacific, Transatlantic, Hawaii, and Panama Canal), the minimum rises to 1 year old . Separately, Disney will refuse passage to anyone who has entered, or will enter, their 24th week of pregnancy by the time the cruise ends. What's the drinking age onboard? 21, on virtually every sailing — U.S. law governs the ship on any cruise departing a U.S. port, regardless of where you are at sea. The one real exception: on select cruises departing certain overseas ports (parts of Europe, and round-trip sailings from Australia, New Zealand, or Singapore), guests 18–20 may be permitted to drink, sometimes only with a signed parental consent form. If you're sailing from the U.S., plan around 21 without exception. Can I bring my own alcohol onboard? Yes, but the policy tightened in June 2026. Guests 21+ may now bring one unopened bottle of wine or champagne, plus six beers , packed in carry-on luggage at embarkation only. This is down from the previous allowance of two bottles, and you can no longer replenish your alcohol allotment at each port — that used to be allowed and no longer is. You can still buy alcohol at a port stop, but Disney holds it until the end of the cruise rather than letting you bring it onboard immediately. Will I get seasick? For most people, no. Modern cruise ships (including every DCL ship) have stabilizers that largely eliminate side-to-side rolling, and DCL's larger ships in particular are quite stable in typical Caribbean and Bahamas conditions. If you're prone to motion sickness, the ship's medical center can provide remedies, and booking a stateroom on a lower, more midship deck (see each ship's stateroom guide) minimizes motion further. What's actually included in the cruise fare, and what isn't? Included: your stateroom, all rotational dining, entertainment, youth clubs, and most private-island beach access including the BBQ lunch. Not included: gratuities, specialty dining (Palo, Remy, Enchanté), alcohol, Wi-Fi, spa services, and excursions. See the full cost breakdown for real numbers on each of these. How far in advance should I book? Earlier than most first-time cruisers expect. Popular sailings (school breaks, holiday weeks) and the best stateroom categories can sell out 9–12 months ahead, and Castaway Club returning-guest booking windows open even earlier for repeat cruisers. Booking early also means more time for the price-monitoring benefit a travel agent provides (see our Travel Agents page ) to actually pay off if the fare drops before you sail. Is Wi-Fi included? Basic connectivity for iMessage, WhatsApp, and the Disney Cruise Line Navigator app is free. Real browsing, email, or streaming requires a paid Wi-Fi package, tiered by speed and data allowance — see the cost breakdown page for current pricing. What if I'm a solo parent traveling with one child? This isn't a DCL-specific restriction — a single parent or guardian can absolutely book and sail with their child, no special documentation required beyond the usual proof of citizenship for both of you. If a child is traveling with only one parent and that could raise a custody question at security or immigration in some ports, some experienced cruisers recommend carrying a simple signed permission note from the non-traveling parent, though DCL itself doesn't require it for standard sailings. pages.description: Everything to know about Pirate Night on Disney Cruise Line — the deck party, fireworks at sea, what to wear, and the best spots to watch from.
pages.body: Disney Cruise Pirate Night Guide (2026) | Cruising Cove Cruising Cove Ships Ports Dining Entertainment Excursions FAQ Community Marketplace Find an Agent Onboard traditions Pirate Night. A themed dinner, a deck party, and fireworks at sea — Disney is the only cruise line in the world authorized to do it. — Quick facts At a glance Included on Most Caribbean/Bahamas sailings, 3+ nights Not included on Alaska, Northern Europe Dress code Pirate-themed, optional Party time Usually ~10:15-10:30pm Best viewing decks 12-13, midship or aft Fireworks side Starboard — What it is The evening, start to finish Pirate Night is a themed evening featured on most Caribbean and Bahamas Disney sailings of three nights or longer — it's not offered on Alaska or Northern Europe itineraries due to local regulations. The evening includes a pirate-themed dinner menu, character meet-and-greets with Disney characters in pirate costume (including rarer appearances from Captain Hook and Mr. Smee), and builds to a deck party and fireworks show late in the evening. On the newer Wish-class ships (Wish, Treasure, Destiny), the deck party is called the Pirates Rockin' Parlay Party — live music, special effects, and appearances from Captain Redd and Captain Jack Sparrow himself, set to the Pirates of the Caribbean soundtrack. — Worth knowing Fireworks at sea Disney Cruise Line is the only cruise line in the world authorized to set off fireworks at sea — it's a genuine point of pride for the line and the highlight of the night. Fireworks launch from the starboard side (the right side facing forward), so that's where you want to be. The best viewing spots are upper decks 12 or 13, midship or toward the aft — avoid the port (left) side, where you'll see little to nothing. — For younger kids If you're worried the fireworks noise will overwhelm a young child, you can watch from the interior windows on decks 4 and 5, or from your stateroom balcony if it's on the starboard side. — What to wear Dress code Dressing up is completely optional — you won't be the only one in regular clothes if you'd rather skip it. That said, most guests wear at least one accessory, often just the free red bandana provided in your stateroom. For a fuller look: flowy shirts, vests, sashes, and eye patches for adults; mini pirate hats, vests, or a themed t-shirt for kids. Comfortable shoes matter more than the costume itself — you'll be standing for the deck party and fireworks. Costumes and accessories are available to buy onboard, but they run expensive. Packing your own from home (or a low-cost Etsy find) is the better move. — Planning tips Making the most of it Check the Navigator app for your specific sailing's party time — it's usually around 10:15 or 10:30pm but varies Head to your viewing spot early; the deck gets crowded fast once the party starts There are typically two deck shows plus a Club Pirate dance party before the Pirates of the Caribbean film plays on FunnelVision On the Disney Wish, watch for the atrium chandelier turning red to help set the mood Need costume ideas and what else to pack? The fare on your booking confirmation is the starting number, not the total. Here's what actually gets added on before you're back home. — Quick facts At a glance Base fare, verandah, 7-night varies by ship/season Gratuities, standard $16/night per guest Gratuities, concierge $27.75/night per guest Palo / Palo Steakhouse ~$50-55/person Wi-Fi, basic tier $16-24/day Bar drinks $10-15 + 18% gratuity — The honest number What's actually included in the fare Your base fare covers the stateroom, all rotational dining (main dining rooms and the buffet), entertainment, youth clubs, and most beach access at the private islands, including the BBQ lunch. That's genuinely a lot — more all-inclusive than most mainstream cruise lines. But gratuities, specialty dining, alcohol, Wi-Fi, spa services, and excursions are all separate , and none of them show up in the sticker price you book against. — Watch From Founding Cruise Experts Budget and packing breakdowns from creators featured on Cruising Cove. — The real add-ons Where the extra spending actually goes Gratuities. Disney's recommended standard gratuity is $16.00 per person, per night, covering your stateroom host and dining team. Concierge staterooms and suites recommend $27.75 per person, per night. For a family of four on a 7-night sailing in a standard stateroom, that's roughly $448 in gratuities alone — easy to overlook if you're only budgeting the fare. These can be prepaid before sailing or settled onboard. Specialty dining. Palo (or Palo Steakhouse on the newer ships) runs roughly $50–55 per person for brunch or dinner. Remy and Enchanté run higher, as fine-dining venues with a prix-fixe format. A gratuity is added separately to these bills, on top of the meal price. Wi-Fi. Free basic connectivity covers iMessage, WhatsApp, and the Navigator app. Real internet access is tiered: roughly $16–18/day for social-media-only access, $24–28/day for browsing and email, with a premium tier priced higher still for full streaming speed. Alcohol. Individual drinks run $10–15 plus an automatic 18% gratuity. You're allowed to bring aboard two bottles of wine or six beers per adult at embarkation and at each port, which is the main way experienced cruisers manage this cost. Excursions. Disney's own Port Adventures range from roughly $50 to $300+ per person depending on the activity — a real budget swing depending on how many stops you book activities at. — Next Pack for the climate, not just the fare Once the budget is sketched, use the Disney cruise packing list — destination layers, Pirate Night, formal nights, Halloween costumes, premium dining, and Disneybound ideas by ship. — Coming soon A real calculator for your sailing — In progress A true all-in cost calculator — where you enter your ship, sail length, party size, and stateroom category and get a realistic total including gratuities, one specialty dinner, a Wi-Fi tier, and a couple of drinks — is one of the tools this site is being built around. Destination extras below layer on top — don’t buy a second suitcase for every port day. Documents & embarkation Passports or birth certificates + photo ID (match Disney’s current document rules for your itinerary) Booking confirmation / Port Arrival Form access (phone or printed backup) Credit card for Key to the World / Folio setup Any medical letters, prescriptions in original bottles Travel insurance info + emergency contacts Cabin comfort Magnetic hooks (metal walls — huge quality-of-life upgrade) Over-door organizer or packing cubes Night light / clip fan if your family runs warm Reusable water bottles (fill at drink stations) Basic first-aid, motion-sickness plan, pain reliever Phone chargers + small power strip (ships have limited outlets) Daytime wardrobe (all itineraries) Comfortable walking shoes + sandals Swimsuits + cover-ups Light layers for AC indoors (ship is cold in theaters & dining rooms) Casual dinner outfits for most rotational nights Workout clothes if you’ll use the gym or run the track Nice-to-haves Lanyards for Key cards (or a marketplace magnetic holder) Small backpack / beach tote for port days Refillable sunscreen (reef-safe where required) Sunglasses + hat Fish Extender gifts if you’re participating in your sailing community Disney provides shampoo, conditioner, body wash, and a hair dryer. Bring your preferred brands if picky — packing space is better spent on layers and shoes. — Warm water Bahamas & Caribbean Most Wish-, Destiny-, Dream-, and Fantasy-class sailings out of Florida and Galveston. Hot sun, humid port days, private-island beach time, and usually a Pirate Night . Add to your bag 2–3 swimsuits per person (they rarely dry overnight in humid cabins) Rash guards / UV shirts for kids Water shoes for rocky beaches & tender ports Quick-dry towels or a compact beach blanket (island chairs exist, but extras help) Insect repellent for some Caribbean ports at dusk Light rain shell — short tropical showers happen Snorkel mask you trust (optional; rentals exist too) Port-day tips Castaway Cay / Lookout Cay: prioritize sunscreen, hats, and a dry change for the ride back Cozumel / Nassau / San Juan: breathable clothing + closed shoes if shopping streets are uneven Keep one “nice casual” outfit clean for sail-away and photo ops Western Caribbean (e.g. Cozumel, Grand Cayman) and Eastern / Bahamas runs pack almost the same — humidity and beach gear win either way. — Cool climate Alaska Layering beats one giant coat. Temperatures swing from cool mornings on deck to warmer afternoons in port — and there’s usually no Pirate Night on these itineraries. Add to your bag Waterproof jacket with a hood Fleece or mid-layer + long pants for most days Warm hat, gloves, and a scarf or neck gaiter for glacier days Broken-in waterproof walking shoes Binoculars for wildlife & scenery Jeans / chinos that can handle damp weather One swimsuit anyway (hot tubs + spa still happen) Skip or downsize Multiple tropical cover-ups Full pirate costume kit (unless you’re dressing up for fun on your own) Heavy formal coats — a sleek layer over dress clothes is enough Excursion days (helicopters, ziplines, glaciers) need grip-friendly shoes more than fashion sneakers. — City + coast Europe & Northern itineraries Think “city walking tour meets cruise ship.” Weather varies by month and route — Mediterranean summers feel Caribbean-adjacent; Northern Europe needs Alaska-style layers. Add to your bag Comfortable walking shoes you’ve already broken in Modest options for churches / historic sites (shoulders & knees covered when needed) Compact umbrella or packable rain jacket Crossbody bag that zips for crowded old towns Adapters if you’re overnighting pre/post cruise in Europe Light sweater for cool evenings and aggressive ship AC Dress-code note Northern Europe sailings typically skip Pirate Night / fireworks at sea You’ll still have rotational dining dress expectations and specialty restaurants Pack one polished outfit for Captain’s Gala / formal-leaning nights if listed on your itinerary — Little sailors Keeping kids entertained Youth clubs are excellent — but embarkation day, tender waits, and quiet cabin time still happen. Pack small, familiar, and non-messy. Cabin & travel days Favorite stuffed animal / comfort item Tablet + headphones with downloads (Wi‑Fi is paid and imperfect) Magnetic games, card games, sticker books Coloring supplies that won’t explode in luggage Snacks for airport / embarkation queues (within cruise food rules) White-noise app or small sound machine for light sleepers Pool, clubs & characters Goggles kids will actually wear Easy on/off cover-ups for Oceaneer Club drop-off Autograph book + fat pens (characters wear gloves) Lanyard for club cards / Key cards Backup outfit after splash pads and soft-serve Register for Oceaneer Club / Edge / Vibe early on embarkation day so you’re not unpacking during the longest line of the cruise. — Them night Pirate Night packing Optional but beloved on most tropical sailings of 3+ nights. pages.h1: Which excursion actually fits your family?
pages.body: Disney Cruise Port Adventures — How to Choose by Port | Cruising Cove Cruising Cove Ships Ports Dining Entertainment Excursions FAQ Community Marketplace Find an Agent Port Adventures Which excursion actually fits your family? Filter by toddler-friendly, wheelchair accessible, adventurous, beach day, budget, or Disney-run vs. independent — then see what that looks like at each common Disney port. — Start here Pick the filter before you pick the tour Most Port Adventure disappointment comes from booking the wrong kind of day — not the wrong operator. Decide which filter matters most for your group, then compare only options that clear it. Family filters Ship-wait rule Examples by port When to book — Family filters Use these filters first Ages 1–4 Toddler-friendly Short transfers, shade, bathrooms nearby, low walking. Skip multi-hour “highlight reels” that keep kids strapped in a van. Mobility Wheelchair / accessible Confirm vehicle lift, path surfaces, and whether the attraction itself is accessible — “accessible tour” sometimes only means the van. High energy Adventurous Snorkel, ATV, zip, kayak. Check age/height minimums and whether non-riders sit around waiting. Swim day Beach day Chair/umbrella included or rental, bathroom distance, soft vs. rocky entry, and how long the transfer eats into swim time. All-in dollars Budget Compare tickets + transfer + tips + time tax, not just the headline price. Sometimes “free beach” beats a cheap tour. Risk tradeoff Disney vs independent Disney costs more; independent is often cheaper. For most families the deciding detail is whether the ship waits if you’re late. — The detail most people miss If you’re late, does the ship wait? Book through Disney and the excursion runs late — the ship waits for you. Book independently and something goes wrong — traffic, a slow boat, a breakdown — and the ship does not wait. You cover getting to the next port yourself. For families with kids, that insurance is often worth more than the price gap. Full decision framework: Disney Port Adventures vs. independent tours . — Port by port What each filter looks like in real ports These are pattern guides — not a catalog of every Disney tour code. pages.title: Castaway Cay Guide
pages.description: A complete guide to Castaway Cay, Disney Cruise Line
pages.body: Castaway Cay Guide | Cruising Cove Cruising Cove Ships Ports Dining Entertainment Excursions FAQ Community Marketplace Find an Agent Private Island · The Bahamas Castaway Cay. Disney's original private island: a protected lagoon, three separate beaches, and a complimentary BBQ lunch included in every stop. — Quick facts At a glance Opened 1998 Location Bahamas Size ~1,000 acres Dock type Direct pier, no tender Beaches 3 Lunch Included, BBQ style — The island What's there Castaway Cay is Disney Cruise Line's private island in the Bahamas, and the ship docks directly at a pier — no tender boat required, which means faster, easier access than most cruise-line private islands. The island is split into three beach areas: two family beaches (connected by tram and walking paths) and Serenity Bay, reserved for guests 18 and older. The water throughout is shallow and calm, protected by a breakwater, which makes it easy and safe for young kids. A complimentary BBQ lunch is served at both the family beaches and Serenity Bay between roughly 11:30am and 2:00pm — grilled chicken, burgers, hot dogs, fish, and sides, with non-alcoholic drinks included. You never have to return to the ship for lunch, though the option is there if you'd rather. — Free to do Included activities Pelican Plunge — a free floating inflatable water play structure just off the family beach Snorkeling in the designated lagoon, including sunken Disney-themed props A 5K running course around the island (free, self-guided) Hammocks, lounge chairs, and umbrellas throughout all three beaches Character meet-and-greets in tropical attire — check the Navigator app for times Massage cabanas at Serenity Bay (booked through the onboard spa, extra cost) — Worth booking early Cabanas Castaway Cay has 20 private cabanas split between the family beach and Serenity Bay — roughly 325 square feet each, with lounge chairs, a hammock, a stocked cooler, and complimentary snorkel gear. Family beach cabanas run roughly $450–600/day; Serenity Bay cabanas start around $600+/day. They're genuinely worth it for a large group wanting guaranteed shade and privacy, but they sell out within minutes of the booking window opening — typically 75 days before sailing for the general public, earlier for higher Castaway Club tiers. — Coming soon A day-by-day countdown showing exactly when your cabana booking window opens, based on your sail date and Castaway Club tier, is part of what this site is being built to do. — Worth knowing Planning tips Bring your stateroom key card and comfortable shoes if you plan to run the 5K Beach towels are provided at the pier — no need to pack your own The family beaches get crowded near the tram stop; walking 5–10 minutes further usually finds quieter spots Food is free at both BBQ locations; bar drinks and specialty items are not — Watch From Founding Cruise Experts Port walkthroughs and tips from creators featured on Cruising Cove. pages.body: Lookout Cay at Lighthouse Point Guide | Cruising Cove Cruising Cove Ships Ports Dining Entertainment Excursions FAQ Community Marketplace Find an Agent Private Peninsula · Eleuthera, Bahamas Lookout Cay at Lighthouse Point. Disney's second Bahamian destination, opened in 2024 — built around authentic Bahamian culture rather than classic Disney theming, with one of the best beaches in the fleet's ports. — Quick facts At a glance Opened June 2024 Location Eleuthera, Bahamas Size ~700 acres Distance from Castaway Cay ~120 miles Beaches 2 (family + Serenity Bay) Kids club Sebastian's Cove, ages 3-10 — The island What's different here Lookout Cay at Lighthouse Point sits on a peninsula on the southern tip of Eleuthera — not a fully private island like Castaway Cay, but a privately controlled section of a larger, inhabited island. Disney purchased the property in 2019 and opened it to guests in June 2024. Where Castaway Cay leans into classic Disney character theming, Lookout Cay is built around Bahamian culture, art, and conservation, including a Goombay Cultural Center celebrating Junkanoo traditions. One real difference worth knowing before you go: Castaway Cay's beaches sit behind a breakwater, so the water is calm and sheltered. Lighthouse Point's beaches are unsheltered, so conditions can be more variable — often beautiful, but worth checking conditions if you're planning to swim with young kids. — What's there Beaches and activities Mabrika Cove — the main family beach, stretching the length of the common area Serenity Bay Beach — the adults-only section, with its own BBQ and the Blue Hole Bar Rush Out Gush Out — a water playground for kids Goombay Cultural Center — live Junkanoo performances and local art Sebastian's Cove — the island's kids' club, ages 3–10 A network of elevated bridges over the coastline, built to protect the natural dune habitat — Worth booking early Cabanas Twenty premium family cabanas are available near the family beach, including four double cabanas for larger groups with massage service add-ons. Six additional adult cabanas are available at Serenity Bay. As with Castaway Cay, these book up fast once the reservation window opens. — Worth knowing Planning tips The ship docks at an open-trestle pier (Turbot Berth) connected to shore by roughly a half-mile walkway — budget extra time to get to the beach compared to Castaway Cay's shorter walk This is still a newer port than Castaway Cay, so expect the experience to keep evolving as Disney adds facilities Some 7-night itineraries stop at both Lookout Cay and Castaway Cay on the same sailing Cruising Cove Ships Ports Dining Entertainment Plan Your Sailing Find an Agent Cruising Cove is an independent planning guide and is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by The Walt Disney Company, Disney Cruise Line, or any of their affiliates. pages.body: Disney Cruise Themed Sailings Guide (2026) | Cruising Cove Cruising Cove Ships Ports Dining Entertainment Excursions FAQ Community Marketplace Find an Agent Themed sailings Not every sailing is the same sailing. Certain dates on certain ships get a full extra layer of theming. Here's what's running in 2026, and which ship and itinerary each one lives on. — Superheroes at sea Marvel Day at Sea For the first time, Marvel Day at Sea moved to the Disney Magic , sailing 4- and 5-night Western Caribbean itineraries out of Galveston, Texas starting January 2026. Over 30 heroes and villains appear across the day, including Spider-Man, Captain America, Captain Marvel, Thor, Loki, and Black Panther — plus a USO-style tribute show honoring Captain America in Fathoms and warrior training with Okoye in the atrium. The day builds to a deck party themed around a clash between heroes and villains. — Pixar pals Pixar Day at Sea Pixar Day at Sea returns on the Disney Fantasy , sailing 5-night Bahamian itineraries from Port Canaveral, Florida, stopping at Nassau, Castaway Cay, and Lookout Cay at Lighthouse Point. Expect appearances from beloved Pixar characters throughout the day, capped off with a Pixar Pals Celebration deck party in the evening. — Seasonal favorites Halloween on the High Seas & Very Merrytime Cruises Halloween on the High Seas runs during the fall season across the fleet, with themed decor, character costumes, and trick-or-treating activities for kids. Very Merrytime Cruises bring holiday theming to U.S.-based DCL ships during the winter season — tree lightings, holiday character appearances, and festive entertainment. Both are seasonal add-ons to regular sailings rather than a separate ship or itinerary. — Character-themed sailings Bluey & other family favorites 2026 also brings Bluey and Bingo–themed experiences to select sailings on the Disney Dream and Disney Wish , aimed at families with younger kids. — Worth knowing What isn't currently running — Status check Star Wars Day at Sea has run on Disney Cruise Line in the past and is frequently requested by fans, but is not part of the confirmed 2026 lineup as of this writing. Worth verifying current availability before booking a sailing specifically for it.
